column2: req_desc

Loading gate.
The page opens on a gate that traces the Stillhour mark and shows "Gathering the evening" with a real loading percentage, then offers "Begin the hour" and "Begin in silence", and nothing scrolls or sounds before one is chosen.

Sound switch.
A "Sound" switch in the top bar starts on or off according to the gate choice, mutes and unmutes all sound with a short fade, and is remembered in this browser, as detailed in Interactions.

Hero title reveal.
After the gate the title "Give your last hour a shape." appears letter by letter over the contour landscape and keeps its full text as its accessible name.

Story clock.
The top-bar story clock reads 21:00 at the top of the page and 22:00 at the very bottom, moving one minute at a time with scroll in both directions.

City window counter.
In the city chapter a counter falls from 4,096 windows to 1 and the caption steps through three lines at fixed points of that chapter's scroll, rising and reverting exactly when the visitor scrolls back.

Numbers band.
The numbers band rolls up 60 minutes, 06 rituals and 01 bedtime and shows the live count of people keeping a Stillhour tonight from the server, or resting copy when the count is unavailable.

Scroll-tied chapters.
The brightness dial falls from 100% to 5%, the settle line's letters sink into place and the moonflowers close with scroll, each reversing on the way up, and a moonflower also closes early when hovered or tapped.

Goodnight footer.
The page ends on the lantern scene, whose flame goes out as the last part of the page scrolls into view, with the word "Goodnight." and the links "Manage my hour" and "Privacy".

Breathing guide.
"Breathe with me" runs three rounds of four seconds in, seven held and eight out, announcing each phase, and "Stop" ends it at once.

Film player.
"Play the film" opens a modal film dialog with a 40-second film and a custom player with play and pause, seek, captions, mute, full screen and keyboard keys, which returns focus to its opener when closed.

Ritual cards.
Chapter four shows the six catalogue rituals as cards with their title, default minutes and a looping clip that plays only while the card is on screen.

Ritual toggles.
Each card's toggle adds or removes its ritual, shows its pressed state and changed label, announces the new total, and refuses a ritual that would take the hour past 60 minutes.

Rituals in the address.
The chosen rituals and their minutes live in the page address, so a reload, a shared address or returning with Back restores the same choices.

Sideways ritual chapter.
On wide screens without reduced motion chapter four pins while the cards travel sideways over a turning moon, and on every other screen the cards stack vertically with no pinning.

Planner form.
The planner collects email, bedtime, time zone, rituals with minutes and a note, and shows the hour's local start time and planned minutes as the visitor edits.

Planner error summary.
Saving with invalid fields shows an error summary whose links move focus to each field, alongside each field's own message, without sending anything.

Save endpoint.
POST /api/plans saves a draft hour and answers 202 with the same body for new and known addresses, as specified in API.

Plan rules.
The server rejects rituals, bedtimes, time zones, notes and extra fields outside the plan rules with 422 naming each offending field.

Note and body limits.
A note of up to 280 characters, counted as a reader sees them, is accepted and a longer one is refused, and a request body over 16,384 bytes is refused with 413.

Idempotent saves.
Repeating a save with the same Idempotency-Key and body within 24 hours returns the first answer without a second draft or email, and a different body under that key answers 409.

Confirmation email.
Each new draft sends one "Confirm your Stillhour" email to its address through the outbox, with a link to /signin carrying a one-time token.

One save per click.
A visitor who double-clicks "Save my hour" or retries after a dropped connection gets one draft, one confirmation email and the saved message in the planner status.

Emailed link lifetime.
Every emailed link works once and expires fifteen minutes after it was sent, answering 404, 410 link_used or 410 link_expired as qualified in Business rules.

Link verification.
POST /api/session/verify with a confirmation token confirms the draft as the address's hour with reminders on, and any valid token signs the visitor in.

Session cookie and sign out.
A successful verification sets the stillhour_session cookie for 30 days, /api/me routes answer 401 signed_out without it, and signing out ends the session.

Live count.
GET /api/tonight returns exactly the number of confirmed hours with reminders on, right after every confirmation, pause, resume and deletion.

Confirm journey.
Opening the confirmation link shows the confirmed message on the sign-in page and then the hour on Manage my hour.

Same reply for every address.
Asking for a sign-in link answers 202 with the same body whether or not the address has a saved hour, and only addresses with a saved hour receive an email.

Hourly link limits.
Saves are limited to 3 and sign-in requests to 5 per address per hour, after which the server answers 429 with Retry-After for every address alike.

Sign-in journey.
On Manage my hour a keeper enters their email, sees the neutral sent message, opens the emailed link and reaches their editor.

Read my hour.
GET /api/me/plan returns the keeper's hour in the published plan shape, including its local start time, next reminder and share link.

Editable fields only.
PATCH /api/me/plan changes only bedtime, time zone, rituals, note and reminders, and refuses any other field with 422 while changing nothing.

Stale edits refused.
An edit without If-Match answers 428 and an edit against an older version answers 409 with the current hour, so a stale tab never overwrites a newer save.

Manage editor.
The signed-in editor saves changes, switches reminders on and off, and on a conflict shows the conflict copy with the latest hour filled in.

Reminder at local start.
Each confirmed hour with reminders on gets a "Your Stillhour starts at <HH:MM>" email at bedtime minus 60 minutes in the hour's own time zone.

Clock-change nights.
On a night when the hour's time zone changes its clocks the keeper still gets exactly one reminder, at the first valid local start as qualified in Business rules.

One reminder per night.
A keeper gets at most one reminder per local night, and a reminder more than 60 minutes late is skipped for that night.

When reminders begin.
Reminders start with the first night whose hour starts at or after the confirmation, the resume or the bedtime or time-zone edit, and a paused hour gets none.

Next reminder shown locally.
Manage my hour shows the next reminder's day and time in the hour's own time zone whatever the browser's time zone, or that reminders are paused.

Test clock.
With STILLHOUR_TEST_CLOCK=1, PUT and DELETE /api/test/clock set and clear the app clock for every instance and run due reminders before answering, and otherwise both answer 404.

Share links.
A keeper can create a share link, replace it with a new one that kills the old, and turn sharing off, after which the old link answers 404.

Shared hour stays private.
A share link shows only bedtime, time zone, rituals and total minutes, never the email or note, and cannot change anything.

Partner view.
A partner opening /p/<token> sees the shared hour read-only, and sees the no-longer-available copy once sharing is off or the hour is deleted.

Delete everything.
DELETE /api/me removes the hour, drafts, links, sessions, share link, unsent emails and future reminders, so nothing more is sent and every old link answers not found.

Delete journey.
On Manage my hour, Delete everything asks the keeper to type DELETE in a dialog before deleting, then shows the deleted message and the sign-in form.

Database outage.
While the database is unreachable every data route answers 503 with the unavailable copy and /api/health still answers 200, and saving works again once the database returns, without a restart.

Mail outage.
While mail is unreachable saves answer confirmation_queued, and every queued email is sent exactly once when mail returns.

Planner during an outage.
A visitor arriving while the database is down still gets the whole story, the resting live-count copy and, on save, the unavailable message with their choices kept.

Run manifest and health.
The app installs, builds and serves from /app/run.json on port 4173 or APP_PUBLIC_PORT and answers GET /api/health with 200 {"status":"ok"}.

Request limits and error shape.
Every API error uses the single published error body, with 405, 415, 400 and 413 answered as published in Server boundary and API.

Same-origin and private internals.
Writes from another origin answer 403 cross_origin, and the server never serves source, configuration or credentials and never shows stack traces, queries or library names.

Credentials from the environment.
Database and mail settings are read from the environment at start, never hard-coded and never sent to the browser.

Keyboard-complete story.
Every control from the gate to the planner and Manage my hour works by keyboard with a visible focus ring, dialogs trap focus, Escape closes them and focus is never lost.

Announced results.
Every ritual change, breathing phase, film state, save, sign-in, share and error result is announced in its named live region with the exact copy from Feedback states.

Three viewports.
At 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 every chapter and control is present and reachable and the page never scrolls sideways.

Reduced motion.
With reduced motion there is no smooth scrolling, pinned sideways section, letter scatter or autoplaying clip, while scenes, clock, counter and captions still follow scroll.

Dusk look.
The page ground darkens chapter by chapter from pale lilac to near-black, with the ember accent kept for light sources and actions and the two named typefaces used throughout.

Story scenes look.
The contour landscape, city, still water, moonflowers, moon and lantern read as one cinematic night on a single fixed canvas behind opaque text chapters.

Code-built scenes and sound.
Every 3D scene is built in code on one canvas without model files, and all sound is decoded from the app's own audio files through one master volume.

Calm forms.
The planner, Manage my hour, the sign-in page and the shared hour are calm two-column or single-column forms in the same dusk style with large touch targets.
Ship /app/run.json with exactly the string fields install, build, serve and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1".

Ship /app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md listing every shipped package, meaning the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json, with its name, version and licence, plus every bundled font and its licence.

Shipped packages (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) use only MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0 or 0BSD licences; fonts use the SIL Open Font License 1.1.
Use no datastore other than the provided PostgreSQL: no SQLite, Redis, embedded database or files written as application state.
Leave the provided service configuration and its development credentials unchanged.
Serve every font, audio file, film, caption track and texture from the app itself; nothing is fetched from a CDN or other origin at runtime.
Write all server and browser source in TypeScript.
